semantic_changes: The scenario driver gained a monotonic-store parameter and an optional repair step; the two new cases use them, and only those two cases are selected for this run.
Two new comparison subjects are recorded: the monotonic case's emptied log store with a persisting claim, and the repair case's stall-then-recovery boundary.

scope.description: Two new cases of the same three-voter history, each built on the unchanged scenario (isolated leader appends entries that never reach a quorum, is shut down, remaining voters elect a leader, commit further entries and take a snapshot, isolated node restarted on its real log store and reconnected). Case one repeats the trimmed configuration with a MonotonicLogStore so the install path deletes the whole log store instead of keeping a suffix above the snapshot index. Case two keeps the non-monotonic store and, once the stall is established, drives the leader's applied index past the follower's cached claim and publishes a snapshot above it, then keeps sampling to see whether the follower resumes accepting entries.
assumptions: Fault model unchanged: no message loss inside the injected transport; the only induced events are a full transport partition of one voter, its clean shutdown and restart on the same stores, and in case two additional client writes plus one forced snapshot on the leader.

Case one uses the captured MockMonotonicLogStore wrapper over InmemStore (IsMonotonic true), so installSnapshot takes the removeOldLogs branch; the leader's own snapshot trimming still uses compactLogs, as in the earlier runs.
Case two adds only: entries applied on the leader until its applied index exceeds the follower's cached claim, then one forced Snapshot(); the stall is measured before those additions.

Reused facilities otherwise unchanged: MakeClusterCustom/MakeClusterOpts with inmemConfig timings, InmemStore, FileSnapshotStore, InmemTransport, MockFSM wrapped by a counting Restore, and the NewRaft restart pattern used by TestRaft_SnapshotRestore_Progress.
excluded: No production logic was modified; the harness only adds test code.
Automatic snapshotting remains disabled (SnapshotThreshold huge, SnapshotInterval 1h) so the leader's snapshot index is controlled by explicit calls in both cases.

basis.prefix: Same scenario driver as the earlier revisions, now parameterised by log-store monotonicity and by an optional repair step. Case one: the trimmed history runs with MonotonicLogs=true; the follower's install deletes its entire log store, and the probe reports whether installs repeat, whether the follower reaches the frontier, whether the cached claim persists, and whether any suffix above the snapshot index survived in the store. Case two: the trimmed history runs as before; when the sample loop passes 1200ms it records the pre-repair applied index, restore count and cluster frontier, keeps applying entries on the leader until its applied index exceeds the follower's cached claim, forces Snapshot() and records the new snapshot index, then continues sampling to 4s and reports whether the stall was present before the repair and whether the follower caught up afterwards.
basis.requirement: A follower that reinstalls the leader's snapshot must remain able to accept subsequent log entries from that leader, or its cached log state must not claim entries the snapshot superseded.

comparisons.description: Monotonic store: the follower's FSM was restored again after the first install, i.e. the same snapshot index was re-shipped during the window with the leader's snapshot index unchanged.
Monotonic store progress predicate: after the window the follower's applied index is still below the cluster frontier although new entries committed and applied elsewhere.
Monotonic store: the follower's cached last log index is still at or beyond the installed snapshot index with a lower term.

Monotonic store: the install branch deleted the whole log store, so no entry above the snapshot index survived, while the cached claim above it persisted - the distinction from the non-monotonic case.
Repair boundary: before the intervention the follower's applied index was below the cluster frontier while repeated restores were being recorded, i.e. the stall was already present.

Repair boundary: after the leader committed past the follower's cached claim and published a snapshot above it, the follower's applied index reached the cluster frontier again, so the stall ends at the claim boundary rather than being permanent.

before.description: Unchanged two-case experiment: two real three-voter cluster histories in one process where a leader is isolated and appends entries that never reach a quorum, is shut down, and the remaining voters elect a leader, commit further entries and take a snapshot; the isolated node is restarted on its unchanged in-memory log store and reconnected. The trimmed case (TrailingLogs=10) can only be repaired by the snapshot; the control (large TrailingLogs) can be repaired by entries. Each case samples restores, applied and commit index, cached last log entry, last snapshot and store range plus the cluster frontier for 3s of steady new writes.

prefix.before: Identical to the previous revision, which ran both cases to completion with the same decisive values: build the cluster with MakeClusterCustom (counting FSM), commit 60 entries, partition the leader, fire 60 applies that never reach a quorum, wait for it to step down, shut it down, wait for one remaining voter to be the only stable leader, commit 20 further entries, force Snapshot(), record the snapshot and trimmed store range, restart the victim with NewRaft on its original stores and a fresh InmemTransport, reconnect it, emit ca_setup with tag plus the premise fields, wait for the first install, sample every 250ms for 3s while applying one entry per sample on the leader, emit ca_probe, then disconnect the victim before bounded teardown.

revision_reason: The third run decided the original five comparisons (all complete and hold), so the harness now covers the two limits that account still states instead of repeating those cases: a monotonic-store variant of the trimmed case, and a repair-boundary case that publishes a snapshot above the follower's cached claim after the stall is established. The scenario driver, stores, restart technique and the earlier cases are kept in the file but only the two new cases are selected for this run; the earlier receipts remain the evidence for the non-monotonic trimmed and control cases.
